note: Tier 1, captured on anthropic-api (2026-10-23, claude-opus-5-5, Messages, OAuth seat): output_config.effort xhigh sent with thinking.type disabled to a model that refuses thinking.type disabled (the same model accepted thinking.type enabled with a 200 the same day). The thinking refusal comes back, not an effort refusal: the message is byte-identical to the thinking-type-disabled-unsupported case and names no effort level. error.message is verbatim; the envelope keeps the captured key order, with the request id field dropped. lifted_type is the error.type routectl lifts from the body.
body: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"\"thinking.type.disabled\" is not supported for this model. Use \"thinking.type.adaptive\" and \"output_config.effort\" to control thinking behavior."}}
